text:
Maria: quick dump of today's perf profile for the selective-per-layer quant work. attaching summary below, want thoughts about excluding embedding + lm_head vs only excluding embed

PerfBot: auto-report: p50 latency down 9%, p95 down 5%, throughput +14% for mixed-int8 w/ selective exclusions. detailed csv at /artifacts/1856/bench-1856007890.csv :robot_face:

Ben: nice. did you run with KV cache enabled? that's been the weird regressor lately

Maria: yes KV enabled. with cache cold start we saw p99 spikes on short sequences when using int4 mid-layer kernels. hypothesis: more memcpy/transpose overhead between quant kernels and cache layout

Sasha: can you paste the kernel selection config you used?

Maria: sure:
```
kernel_selector:
  - layer_range: [0,2]
    quant: fp16
  - layer_range: [3, -3]
    quant: int8
  - layer_range: [-2, -1]
    quant: fp16  # lm_head excluded
  cache_policy: kv-layout=packed
  batcher:
    max_latency_ms: 30
    prefer_contiguous_batches: true
```

Igor: interesting. embedding excluded + lm_head excluded. Did you try excluding only lm_head and keeping embeddings int8?

Maria: did both variants. numbers:
- exclude both: throughput +18%, top-1 quality delta -0.6%
- exclude lm_head only: throughput +16%, quality delta -0.3%
- exclude embedding only: throughput +12%, quality delta -1.1% (embedding exclusion hurts perf more than lm_head exclusion oddly)

Ben: embedding exclusion hurting perf more makes sense if embedding kernels are fused on this GPU stack — forcing fp16 path breaks a large fused matmul and forces extra transfers

Sasha: calibration effects? were these calibrated per-layer or global scale?

Maria: per-layer calibration for int8 and per-channel for fp8 in the baseline. when we switched to global scale for speed we saved ~6% compile/setup time but quality regressed ~0.8% on some LMs

Jess: any KV cache interactions where quantized layers invalidate cache or need reformatting?

Maria: yes: when the runtime switches execution path mid-inference (e.g., first token uses fp16 path then following tokens route to int8 kernels), we observed a tiny serialization point where the KV layout is converted, costing ~1–2ms per conversion. With frequent routing flips (canary-scale routing) that adds up and shows as p99 tail

Igor: that suggests we should prefer stable routing for sessions — maybe pin the execution path after the first few tokens and amortize conversion cost

Ben: also worth trying KV layout variants: separate int8-friendly packed KV vs generic layout. PerfBot benchmarks showed packed KV + int8 gives best steady-state but worse cold-start

Sasha: two quick asks: (1) can we add a short bench that measures cold-start+steady-state separately per-policy; (2) run a small eval set to track quality per-layer exclusion (we need token-level diffs)

Maria: yes I'll wire up a bench that reports cold-start(1-8 tokens) and steady-state(9-256) separately. will also push per-token diff logs. assigning run to @Sasha and @Ben if ok :thumbsup:

Sasha: happy to run. I'll also try a variant where we keep embeddings int8 but force lm_head fp16 and compare KV-layout tradeoffs

Ben: I'll prototype a packed-KV conversion that runs asynchronously during warmup so it doesn't add to request p99. quick spike but might hide conversion cost

PerfBot: note: created ticket RW-1427 for "selective quant bench + kv-layout cold-start" and linked artifact 1856007890. ETA 48h

Maria: perfect. next sync in two days unless someone sees a burning issue. thanks all :rocket:
